clues.text: On the Passover night in Egypt, Israelites dipped a cluster of it in blood to brush their doorframes.
In a psalm pleading for mercy, the writer asks to be purified with it and made whiter than snow.
At the cross, a sponge soaked in sour wine was put on a stalk of it and lifted to Jesus.
Wise King Solomon spoke of plants, from the cedar in Lebanon to this one growing in the wall.
Moses used it with blood, water and scarlet wool to sprinkle the scroll and all the people.
After someone died in a tent, a clean man dipped it in purifying water and sprinkled the tent and people.
To cleanse someone healed of a skin disease, the priest dipped it with a live bird into blood.
